key_insight: SLMs can retain much of an LLM's reasoning power by learning when a local context is 'sufficient' to reason on its own—enabling selective local thinking and drastically reducing expensive external LLM calls.
problem_solved: Bridges the reasoning-performance gap between small language models (SLMs) and large language models (LLMs) without frequent, costly LLM invocations or unattainable full-model distillation.
method: Define a local sufficiency criterion to identify segments where the SLM has enough context to reason correctly.
Train the SLM to selectively perform internal reasoning on locally sufficient segments and defer (or use lightweight proxy) on insufficient ones.
Apply selective distillation/finetuning focused on locally sufficient examples so the SLM internalizes key reasoning steps while minimizing external LLM calls.
impact: Enables lower-latency, lower-cost deployment of more capable SLMs for production and edge use-cases, making advanced reasoning practical on resource-constrained hardware.
visual_elements: Two-panel flowchart: (A) baseline with frequent LLM calls and high latency; (B) Select-to-Think pipeline showing local sufficiency check → local reasoning → occasional external call.
Bar chart comparing latency, cost, and accuracy trade-offs between baseline, standard distillation, and Select-to-Think.
Illustration of a text window highlighting 'locally sufficient' tokens vs. insufficient regions to show how selection works.
Icon set: small model (edge device) with clock/dollar signs vs. large model (cloud) with higher clock/dollar, emphasizing cost/time savings.
paper_title: Select to Think: Unlocking SLM Potential with Local Sufficiency
paper_authors: Wenxuan Ye, Yangyang Zhang, Xueli An, Georg Carle, Yunpu Ma
